Why we're different

Every quote looks the same on handover day.

Two driveways can look identical the afternoon they're finished and be three thousand pounds apart. The difference is buried where you'll never see it. It shows up in year three, not week one. Here's exactly what we put underneath.

Under a driveway

Blocks or porcelain
50mm
Sharp sand laying course
30mm
Compacted MOT Type 1
150mm+
Geotextile membrane
full area

The corner that gets cut is the sub-base: 75mm instead of 150mm, uncompacted, no membrane. It looks perfect for two summers, then ruts under the car and the joints open up.

Under an extension

Screed and finish
75mm
Insulation
to current regs
DPM, lapped to DPC
sealed
Concrete slab and footings
to depth

Footings get dug to the depth the ground actually needs, not the depth that keeps the muck-away bill down. The membrane gets lapped and taped into the wall DPC properly, because damp is unfixable later.

Under a roof

Tiles or slate
new or reclaimed
Treated battens
graded
Breathable membrane
full strip
Rotten deck left in place
the shortcut

A cheap re-roof means tiles over the existing felt and battens. We strip to the rafters, replace anything soft, and you get a roof that's genuinely new rather than resurfaced.

Ask every builder you're quoting to write the build-up into the quote. Depth of sub-base, thickness of concrete, whether the roof is being stripped to the rafters. Any decent builder will put it in writing without hesitating. Then the quotes that suddenly look cheap start to make sense.

Who you're dealing with

A builder who never left the site.

Most building firms of any size put a salesman in front of you, an estimator behind him, and a site manager you meet once. TPS Installations is deliberately built the other way round.

The person who walks your property is the person who prices it, plans it, and turns up in the morning to build it. That means fewer jobs on the books at any one time, and a straight answer when you ask how it's going.

How it runs

From first call to final sweep.

Five stages, no surprises in between. You'll know who's coming, what's happening and what it costs at every point.

  1. The call

    Tell us what you're thinking. If it's not a job we're right for, we'll say so on the phone rather than waste a visit. Where we can, we'll point you at someone who is.

    Same day, usually

  2. Site visit

    We come out and look at it properly: ground conditions, access, drainage, what's already there. This is where the real cost of a job reveals itself, and it's why we won't quote blind over email.

    Within one working day of your enquiry

  3. Planned and priced

    Drawings and pricing are worked up in-house by the person who'll build it. You get a fixed written quotation with the build-up specified: depths, materials, stages. Not a single number on a compliments slip.

    Typically 3 to 5 days

  4. On site

    Work starts on the agreed date with the owner on the tools. Specialist trades are booked in around the programme. Site is swept and made safe every evening, and you get told what's happening tomorrow.

    Staged payments as work completes

  5. Snagged and signed off

    We walk it with you, write down anything you're not happy with, and fix it before the final invoice. Building control sign-off and any certificates are handed over with the keys.

    Final payment only when you're happy

Questions

Everything homeowners ask.

Do you carry out the work yourselves?

Yes. Every job is planned and priced by the owner, and he's on site working it. Where a specialist trade is needed (a roofer for a full strip, a plasterer for a whole-house skim, an electrician for first fix), we bring in people we've worked alongside for years. You deal with the same person throughout, and he's accountable for all of it.

What areas do you cover?

Based in Ferndown and covering most of Dorset: Bournemouth, Poole, Wimborne, Christchurch, Verwood, Ringwood, Wareham and the villages in between. Slightly further out, ask anyway; it depends on the size of the job.

Is the quote fixed, or does it move?

Fixed and in writing. The price only changes if you ask for something extra, or if something genuinely unforeseeable turns up once the ground's open: unrecorded drainage, inadequate existing foundations, rot under a roof deck. If that happens we stop, show you, and agree the cost before continuing. You'll never find out about extra work on the final invoice.

Why is a cheaper quote sometimes a false economy?

Because the savings almost always come from what gets buried. A 75mm sub-base instead of 150mm. Thinner concrete. No membrane. Tiles laid back over failing battens. On handover day the two jobs look identical. The difference shows up in year three, when the driveway ruts or the ceiling stains. Ask every builder quoting you to write the build-up into the quote.

How long does a typical extension take?

A single-storey rear extension is usually eight to twelve weeks from breaking ground to handover. Two-storey work runs longer. The variables are ground conditions, how fast building control can inspect, and lead times on anything bespoke like steels or glazing. You'll get a realistic programme with your quote rather than an optimistic one designed to win the job.

Do you handle planning and building regulations?

The planning side is handled in-house rather than farmed out to a third party. We'll tell you upfront whether your project needs full permission or falls under permitted development, and we'll work to your building control inspector's schedule and be on site for the inspections.

What sub-base do you lay under a driveway?

For a domestic driveway, typically 150mm or more of MOT Type 1 over a geotextile membrane, compacted in layers rather than in a single pass, then a 30mm sharp sand laying course under the blocks or slabs. Falls are set so water runs away from the house.
